blocks.text: 1. Prefix Tuning
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293834-914779082.png

QLoRA's own closing recap, already covered in QLoRA, pointed forward here. Prefix Tuning, another parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach with a different mechanism, moves away from touching weights entirely.
It genuinely prepends trainable vectors to the model's own internal input rather than touching any weights, an idea explored in full throughout this topic.
2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to QLoRA's own closing recap, already covered in QLoRA. Prefix tuning was genuinely previewed there as another parameter-efficient approach with a different mechanism, briefly described in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely gives it the complete, dedicated treatment already promised, exploring every detail already hinted at generally in that earlier topic.
3. Recapping Weight Based Efficiency
This connects back to LoRA, already covered in LoRA. LoRA genuinely stayed efficient by training small, added weight matrices instead of the original ones.
Prefix tuning genuinely takes an entirely different route: leaving genuinely all weights completely alone, a genuinely fundamental contrast explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Trainable Continuous Vectors
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293834-690692191.png
This connects back to recapping weight-based efficiency, already covered in this topic. Prefix tuning genuinely introduces a small set of trainable continuous vectors instead of touching any weight.
These genuinely are not real words at all, just genuinely free-form numeric vectors learned during training, a genuinely important distinction explored throughout the rest of this topic.
5. Prepending To The Input Sequence
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293834-466405532.png

This connects back to trainable continuous vectors, already covered in this topic. Those genuinely trainable vectors get prepended directly in front of the real input sequence, already covered generally in Prompting.
The genuinely entire model architecture and every genuinely original weight stays completely frozen and unchanged, a genuinely direct parallel to LoRA's own frozen base, already covered in LoRA.
6. Influencing Attention Without Changing Weights
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293834-598995491.png

This connects back to prepending to the input sequence, already covered in this topic. Because self-attention, already covered generally in Attention Mechanism, attends over every token, the prefix genuinely influences every later computation.

This genuinely steers the frozen model's own behavior without ever genuinely modifying a single weight, the exact mechanism by which prefix tuning actually works, explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This attention-based influence, already covered in this topic, directly explains why the prefix must genuinely be placed at the very start of the sequence, so every later token's own attention computation genuinely sees it.

blocks.text: 7. Extremely Few Trainable Parameters
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446294094-466199589.png

This connects back to influencing attention without changing weights, already covered in this topic. The trainable prefix genuinely represents a genuinely tiny fraction of the model's own total parameter count.
It is often genuinely even smaller than LoRA's own already-small trainable matrix pair, already covered in LoRA, a genuinely extreme level of efficiency explored throughout the rest of this topic.

10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates prepending a trainable prefix to an input sequence, already covered in this topic, before it reaches a frozen model.

code.content:
import random
random.seed(0)

def random_vector(dim=4):
    return [round(random.uniform(-1, 1), 2) for _ in range(dim)]

# already covered as trainable continuous vectors in this topic
prefix_length = 3
trainable_prefix = [random_vector() for _ in range(prefix_length)]
print(f"Trainable prefix vectors (already covered in this topic): {trainable_prefix}")

def token_embedding(token):
    # already covered as embedding lookup, generally covered elsewhere in this course
    random.seed(hash(token) % 1000)
    return random_vector()

real_input = ["translate", "hello", "to", "french"]  # already covered generally in Prompting
real_embeddings = [token_embedding(t) for t in real_input]

# already covered as prepending to the input sequence in this topic
full_sequence = trainable_prefix + real_embeddings
print(f"\nFull sequence length after prepending (already covered in this topic): {len(full_sequence)}")
print(f"First {prefix_length} entries are the genuinely trainable prefix; the rest are the frozen model's real input")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Prefix tuning prepends trainable vectors to the input rather than touching any model weight.
Unlike LoRA, it introduces no added weight matrices at all; the model stays entirely untouched.
The trainable vectors are not real words, just free-form numeric vectors learned during training.
They get prepended in front of the real input sequence, before it reaches the frozen model.
Because self-attention attends over every token, the prefix influences every later computation.
This lets the prefix steer the frozen model's behavior without modifying a single weight.
The trainable prefix is often even smaller than LoRA's own already-small trainable matrix pair.
This extreme efficiency comes with a real tradeoff: prefix tuning often slightly underperforms LoRA.
